La lumière du Soleil, à 150 millions de: Sunlight, from 150 million km away, takes about 8 minutes to reach us.
7 unités de base (m, kg, s, A, K, mol, c: 7 base units (m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd). Since 2019, all defined by constants of nature.
Le Système international repose sur sept: The International System rests on seven base units: the metre, the kilogram, the second, the ampere, the kelvin, the mole and the candela. All the others are derived from them: the newton is a kg·m/s², the joule a newton times a metre, the watt a joule per second.
Depuis 1889, le kilogramme était un obje: From 1889 the kilogram was an object: a platinum-iridium cylinder kept at Sèvres. Problem: its copies drifted relative to it, by up to 20 micrograms a year, with no way of telling which was changing. Since 20 May 2019, no unit depends on an object any more: the kilogram is defined by fixing the exact value of the Planck constant, as the metre is by the speed of light.
Les préfixes et le piège des carrés: Prefixes and the trap of squares
Préfixes par mille (k, M, G, T ; m, µ, n: Prefixes go by thousands (k, M, G, T; m, µ, n). For an area the prefix is squared; for a volume, cubed.
Le piège, ce sont les surfaces et les vo: The trap is areas and volumes: the prefix is squared or cubed too. 1 km² is 1,000 × 1,000 = 1,000,000 m². 1 m³ is 100 × 100 × 100 = 1,000,000 cm³. And 1 litre is a cube with 10 cm sides, 1 dm³.
La sonde perdue pour une unité: The probe lost over a unit
Toujours écrire l'unité. Masse (kg) ≠ po: Always write the unit. Mass (kg) ≠ weight (N): on the Moon, same mass, weight divided by 6.
A value without a unit means nothing. In September 1999 the Mars Climate Orbiter probe got too close to Mars and vanished. The cause: ground software supplied impulses in pound-force seconds, imperial units, while another program read them as newton seconds. A factor of 4.45 apart, and a probe lost.
Autre confusion fréquente : la masse et: Another common confusion: mass and weight. Mass, in kilograms, is the amount of matter; it does not change from one world to another. Weight, in newtons, is the force with which a world pulls on you. On the Moon an astronaut keeps their mass, but their weight is divided by about six.
Le mouvement n'a pas besoin de moteur: Motion does not need an engine
Sans force nette, la vitesse ne change p: With no net force, velocity does not change (1st law). A force changes motion; it does not keep it going.
Une balle lancée n'emporte donc pas de «: So a thrown ball does not carry a "force of the throw": once released, only its weight and the air act on it. And the Moon does not fall because the Earth pulls it while letting it fly on: without gravity, inertia would send it off in a straight line.
F = m × a (2e loi). Action et réaction s: F = m × a (2nd law). Action and reaction are equal, opposite, and act on two different objects (3rd law).
La deuxième loi dit ce que fait une forc: The second law says what a force does: it accelerates, and less so the more massive the object. F = m × a: 20 newtons accelerate 10 kg at 2 m/s². Newton stated it in 1687 in the Principia, but in words; Euler wrote it as an equation in the 18th century.
La troisième loi : quand A pousse B, B p: The third law: when A pushes B, B pushes A with the same force, in the opposite direction. The two forces act on two different objects, which is why they do not cancel out. A rocket pushes its gases backwards, the gases push the rocket forwards; no air is needed to push against.
Dans le vide, tout tombe ensemble (g ≈ 9: In a vacuum, everything falls together (g ≈ 9.8 m/s²). Speed = g × t, distance = ½ g t².
Sans air, tous les objets tombent avec l: Without air, all objects fall with the same acceleration, about 9.8 m/s² at the Earth's surface, whatever their mass. On 2 August 1971, on the Moon, Apollo 15 astronaut David Scott dropped a hammer and a falcon feather together: they hit the ground at the same time.
Après une seconde de chute libre, un obj: After one second of free fall, an object is moving at about 9.8 m/s, but has only fallen 4.9 m: speed grows with time, distance with the square of time. On Earth, it is the air that slows the feather, not its lightness.
L'énergie se conserve et change de forme: Energy is conserved and changes form. Joule (1845): heat is a form of energy. No efficiency above 100 %.
L'énergie ne se crée pas et ne disparaît: Energy is neither created nor destroyed: it changes form. Water at the top of a dam has potential energy, m g h; as it falls it converts it into motion, then the turbine into electricity, then your lamp into light and heat.
Il a fallu prouver que la chaleur en fai: It had to be proved that heat is part of it. In 1845 James Joule showed that the same amount of mechanical work, spent as friction in water, always warms it by the same amount: heat and work are two forms of the same thing. That is why no machine can give back more than 100 % of what it receives: perpetual motion does not exist.
Deux fois plus vite, quatre fois plus d': Twice as fast, four times the energy
Énergie cinétique = ½ m v² : vitesse × 2: Kinetic energy = ½ m v²: speed × 2 → energy × 4 → braking distance × 4.
L'énergie de mouvement, l'énergie cinéti: The energy of motion, kinetic energy, is ½ m v². It grows with the square of the speed: at 100 km/h a car does not have twice the energy it has at 50 km/h, but four times.
Cette énergie, les freins doivent la tra: The brakes must turn that energy into heat. For the same braking force, the braking distance is therefore also multiplied by four when speed doubles. Leibniz was already measuring a body's "living force" by m v² in 1686; Coriolis added the ½ in 1829, so that its change exactly equals the work of the forces.
Puissance = énergie ÷ temps (W = J/s). k: Power = energy ÷ time (W = J/s). kWh = energy: 1 kWh = 3.6 million J.
La puissance est un débit d'énergie : 1: Power is a flow of energy: 1 watt is 1 joule per second. A 10 W bulb uses 10 joules every second; a 2,000 W heater, two hundred times more.
Le kilowattheure de votre facture n'est: The kilowatt-hour on your bill is not a power but an energy: a power sustained over a time. 1 kWh = 1,000 W × 3,600 s = 3.6 million joules. The 10 W bulb left on for 100 hours uses 1 kWh. The calories on food labels are energy too: one kilocalorie is about 4,184 joules.
Une onde transporte de l'énergie, pas de: A wave carries energy, not matter
Vitesse = longueur d'onde × fréquence ;: Speed = wavelength × frequency; frequency = 1 ÷ period. Sound ≈ 340 m/s in air, nothing in a vacuum.
Quand une vague passe, le bouchon monte: When a wave passes, the cork goes up and down but does not travel with it. A wave carries energy without carrying matter away. Its speed is its wavelength times its frequency, and frequency is the inverse of the period: a period of 0.01 s gives 100 Hz.
Visible : 400 nm (violet) à 700 nm (roug: Visible: 400 nm (violet) to 700 nm (red). Blue sky: air scatters short wavelengths far more (Rayleigh).
La lumière visible va d'environ 400 nm,: Visible light runs from about 400 nm, violet, to 700 nm, red. Beyond that the eye sees nothing: ultraviolet and X-rays on one side, infrared, microwaves and radio waves on the other. They are all electromagnetic waves, differing only in wavelength.
Les molécules d'air diffusent la lumière: Air molecules scatter light more strongly the shorter its wavelength, as the inverse fourth power: that is Rayleigh scattering, described by Lord Rayleigh from 1871. Blue is therefore sent in every direction far more than red, and the sky looks blue. At sunset, light crosses a lot of air, loses its blue on the way, and the sun turns red.
Source qui approche : fréquence plus hau: Approaching source: higher frequency; receding: lower (Doppler, 1842). Used in radars and astronomy.
Une ambulance qui s'approche paraît plus: An approaching ambulance sounds higher, then lower as it moves away. When the source moves forward, it catches up with its own waves and bunches them: the received frequency goes up. When it moves away, it stretches them: the frequency goes down. That is the Doppler effect, proposed by Christian Doppler in 1842 and tested with sound by Buys Ballot in 1845.
Le même effet vaut pour la lumière et le: The same effect applies to light and radio waves. Police radars measure a car's speed from the frequency shift of the reflected wave. And astronomers read in the red or blue shift of a star's light whether it is moving away or approaching.
Une force étalée sur une surface: A force spread over an area
Pression = force ÷ surface. Sous l'eau :: Pressure = force ÷ area. Under water: +1 bar every 10 m, whatever the shape of the container (Stevin, 1586).
La pression, c'est une force divisée par: Pressure is a force divided by an area. A needle pierces skin with a tiny force because its tip is minute; snowshoes carry the same weight over a large area, and you no longer sink in.
Sous l'eau, chaque mètre ajoute le poids: Under water, every metre adds the weight of the water above: about 1 bar every 10 metres, one more atmosphere. Simon Stevin showed in 1586 that this pressure depends only on the height of liquid, not the shape of the container. At 30 m a diver is therefore under about 4 bars: 1 for the air, 3 for the water.
L'air pèse : baromètre de Torricelli (16: Air has weight: Torricelli's barometer (1643), Puy de Dôme (1648), Magdeburg hemispheres (1654). ≈ 1,013 hPa at sea level.
L'air aussi pèse. En 1643, Evangelista T: Air has weight too. In 1643 Evangelista Torricelli turned a tube full of mercury upside down in a basin: the column dropped and settled at about 76 cm. Above it, a vacuum; what holds the column up is the air pressing on the basin. He had just invented the barometer.
En 1648, à la demande de Pascal, son bea: In 1648, at Pascal's request, his brother-in-law Florin Périer took the barometer to the top of the Puy de Dôme: the column dropped by about 8 cm there, because there is less air above. In 1654 Otto von Guericke pumped the air out from between two copper hemispheres at Magdeburg: two teams of horses could not pull them apart. At sea level, air presses with about 1,013 hPa.
Poussée d'Archimède = poids du fluide dé: Buoyancy = weight of the displaced fluid. It floats if it is less dense than the liquid, on average.
Tout corps plongé dans un fluide reçoit: Any body immersed in a fluid gets an upward push equal to the weight of the fluid it displaces. An object floats if its average density is lower than that of the liquid. A steel liner floats because its hull is full of air; a submarine dives by filling its ballast tanks with water, and surfaces by blowing them out with compressed air.
Et le « Eurêka » ? L'histoire du bain et: And "Eureka"? The story of the bath and King Hiero's crown first appears in writing two centuries later, in Vitruvius, and several historians doubt it: measuring the overflow of water would have been too imprecise for the time. A balance, with the crown and a bar of pure gold immersed in water, would however have been enough to expose the fraud.
Température et chaleur, ce n'est pas par: Temperature and heat are not the same
Température = agitation ; chaleur = éner: Temperature = jiggling; heat = transferred energy. Q = m × c × ΔT, with c = 4,184 J/(kg·°C) for water.
La température mesure l'agitation des pa: Temperature measures how much particles jiggle; heat is energy passing from one body to another. A spark is very hot but holds little heat; a lukewarm bath holds far more. In the 18th century heat was believed to be an invisible fluid, caloric; Rumford and then Joule showed it is a form of energy.
Pour chauffer 1 kg d'eau de 1 °C, il fau: To heat 1 kg of water by 1 °C takes about 4,184 joules: Q = m × c × ΔT. Taking a litre from 20 to 100 °C therefore needs 1 × 4,184 × 80 ≈ 335,000 J; with a 1,000 W hotplate, which supplies 1,000 J per second, it takes about 335 s, a little over five and a half minutes. And if metal feels colder than wood at the same temperature, it is because it draws heat from your hand faster.
1er principe : l'énergie se conserve. 2e: 1st law: energy is conserved. 2nd law: heat flows by itself from hot to cold (Clausius).
Premier principe : l'énergie se conserve: First law: energy is conserved. A machine can convert heat into work, never make it from nothing. Second law: heat flows spontaneously from hot to cold, never the other way, as Rudolf Clausius put it in the 19th century.
Un réfrigérateur ne viole pas cette règl: A fridge does not break that rule: it pumps heat from the inside to the outside by using electricity, and that is why its back gets warm. Without spending energy, cold cannot be made.
Carnot, l'entropie et l'œuf cassé: Carnot, entropy and the broken egg
Rendement limité par l'écart de températ: Efficiency limited by the temperature gap (Carnot, 1824). Entropy: S = k log W (Boltzmann); it does not decrease in an isolated system.
En 1824, Sadi Carnot, jeune ingénieur de: In 1824 Sadi Carnot, a 28-year-old engineer, asked what limits steam engines. His answer: a heat engine takes heat from a hot source, turns part of it into work, and must give the rest back to a cold source. Its maximum efficiency depends only on the temperature difference between the two. None can convert it all.
Plus tard, Clausius invente l'entropie,: Later Clausius invented entropy, and Ludwig Boltzmann explained it: it measures the number of ways to arrange the particles without changing anything we see, S = k log W, a formula engraved on his grave in Vienna. In an isolated system it does not decrease. A broken egg has vastly more possible arrangements than a whole one: that is why it does not put itself back together.
Une vitesse que personne ne rattrape: A speed nobody catches up with
Même vitesse de la lumière pour tous (Ei: Same speed of light for everyone (Einstein, 1905). Time slows for a fast clock. E = mc².
En 1887, Michelson et Morley cherchent à: In 1887 Michelson and Morley tried to measure the Earth's motion through the "aether", the medium supposed to carry light. They found nothing: light goes at the same speed in all directions. In 1905 Einstein, a clerk at the patent office in Bern, made it a principle: the speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all observers, 299,792,458 m/s.
La conséquence est vertigineuse : si la: The consequence is dizzying: if the speed of light does not change, then time and lengths adjust. A fast-moving clock ticks more slowly. And nothing with mass can reach that speed: the energy needed would become infinite. E = mc² also says a little mass is worth an enormous amount of energy, because c² is huge.
Mesuré en 1971 avec des horloges atomiqu: Measured in 1971 with atomic clocks on planes. GPS: about 38 µs of gain per day to correct, otherwise around ten km of error.
En octobre 1971, Joseph Hafele et Richar: In October 1971 Joseph Hafele and Richard Keating took four caesium atomic clocks on airliners, once eastward, once westward, then compared them with clocks left on the ground. Eastward they had lost about 59 billionths of a second; westward they had gained about 273. That is what relativity predicted, within the experiment's precision.
Votre GPS en dépend. Les horloges des sa: Your GPS depends on it. The satellites' clocks run ahead by about 45.8 microseconds a day because they are higher in the gravity field, and fall behind by about 7.2 because they move fast: about 38 microseconds net gain. Without correction, the position would drift by about ten kilometres a day. The clocks are therefore set slightly slow before launch.
Relativité générale (1915) : la masse co: General relativity (1915): mass curves spacetime. Confirmed by the 1919 eclipse and gravitational waves (2015).
En 1915, Einstein va plus loin : la grav: In 1915 Einstein went further: gravity is not a force acting at a distance but a curving of spacetime by mass. Matter tells spacetime how to curve; spacetime tells matter how to move. The Earth does not circle the Sun because it is pulled, but because it follows the straightest possible line in a curved space.
Les preuves s'accumulent. En 1919, penda: The evidence piled up. In 1919, during an eclipse, Arthur Eddington's team measured that starlight is bent near the Sun, twice as much as Newton predicted. And in 2015 the LIGO detectors picked up gravitational waves for the first time, ripples in spacetime from the merger of two black holes.
E = h f : l'énergie va par paquets (Plan: E = h f: energy comes in packets (Planck, 1900). Photons (Einstein, 1905). Atomic energy levels (Bohr, 1913).
En 1900, pour expliquer la lumière émise: In 1900, to explain the light given off by hot bodies, Max Planck assumed energy is exchanged only in packets, quanta, of energy E = h f, proportional to frequency. He saw it as a calculation trick. In 1905 Einstein took them seriously: light is made of grains, photons. This explained the photoelectric effect, and earned him the 1921 Nobel Prize, not relativity.
En 1913, Niels Bohr applique l'idée à l': In 1913 Niels Bohr applied the idea to the atom: the electron is allowed only certain energy levels. Dropping down a level, it emits a photon of a precise colour. That is why each element has its light signature, its lines, which tell us what distant stars are made of.
Les particules arrivent une par une, mai: Particles arrive one by one, but interfere like waves. The wave gives probabilities (Born).
Envoyez des électrons un par un vers une: Send electrons one by one towards a plate with two slits. Each arrives at a precise point on the screen, like a grain. But after thousands of hits, they draw interference fringes, like a wave that went through both slits at once. The experiment was carried out with single electrons in 1974, then in 1989.
C'est la dualité onde-particule. L'onde: That is wave-particle duality. The wave does not say where the particle is, but where it is likely to be. In 1926 Einstein wrote to Max Born that God does not play dice: he never accepted this fundamental randomness. Experiments since then have proved Born right.
Position et vitesse ne peuvent être tout: Position and velocity cannot both be known perfectly (Heisenberg, 1927): it is a property of nature.
En 1927, Werner Heisenberg montre qu'on: In 1927 Werner Heisenberg showed that you cannot know both the position and the velocity of a particle with perfect precision. The sharper one is, the blurrier the other. It is not a flaw in the instruments: that is how nature is made.
Cette physique étrange fait tourner le m: This strange physics runs the modern world. The tunnel effect, which lets a particle cross a barrier it should not be able to pass, explains alpha radioactivity and makes flash memory work. The laser relies on stimulated emission, predicted by Einstein in 1917. And Schrödinger's cat, in 1935, was a criticism: Schrödinger wanted to show the absurdity of applying superposition to an everyday object.
Les préfixes comptent par mille : kilo 1: Prefixes count in thousands: kilo 10³, mega 10⁶, giga 10⁹, tera 10¹²; and the other way milli 10⁻³, micro 10⁻⁶, nano 10⁻⁹. Kilo and milli date from the law of 18 Germinal Year III, 7 April 1795, which created the metric system; mega and micro arrived in 1873, tera and nano in 1960. An order of magnitude is the nearest power of 10: a human is about 1 m, a cell 10 µm, an atom 0.1 nm.
Pendant deux mille ans, on a cru qu'un o: For two thousand years people believed a moving object stops when you stop pushing it. That is what we see every day, because of friction. Galileo, then Newton, turned the idea around: with no net force, an object keeps its speed, in a straight line, forever. That is Newton's first law, the principle of inertia. Newton stated it in 1687, at the start of his Principia, among the "axioms or laws of motion".
Le son est une onde de pression qui a be: Sound is a pressure wave that needs a medium: about 340 m/s in air, nearly 1,500 m/s in water, nothing in a vacuum. Light crosses a vacuum at nearly 300,000 km/s. Hence the storm calculation: 3 seconds between lightning and thunder is about 1 km. The method is old: around 1630, Father Marin Mersenne timed the delay between the flash of a gunshot and its bang, over a known distance.
